CausalChain: HepG2 cells grown in traditional 2D conditions → limited cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions → reduced activation of mechanotransductive pathways (such as Wnt/β-catenin) → epigenetic suppression of drug-metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYPs) → suboptimal in vitro metabolism modeling. Transition to a three-dimensional culture environment → enhanced intercellular signaling and extracellular matrix interactions → activation of Wnt/β-catenin and other mechanosensitive pathways → epigenetic reprogramming that lifts repression on CYP gene promoters → increased expression and activity of drug-metabolizing enzymes.
Hypothesis: Culturing HepG2 cells in a three-dimensional scaffold environment will activate mechanotransductive signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, leading to epigenetic reprogramming that restores cytochrome P450 expression and improves their fidelity as a model for human hepatocyte drug metabolism.
Abstract: HepG2 cells are widely used as an in vitro model system in liver research; however, their limited expression of key cytochrome P450 enzymes and other drug‐metabolizing proteins has raised questions regarding their predictive value for normal hepatocyte function. Recent studies comparing genomic, transcriptomic, and proteomic profiles between HepG2, primary hepatocytes, and other tumor‐derived liver cell lines indicate that HepG2 cells retain distinct epigenetic signatures associated with their hepatoblastoma origin. In this context, the three-dimensional culture environment has been demonstrated to enhance cellular interactions and recapitulate in vivo-like architecture, potentially activating mechanotransduction pathways such as Wnt/β‐catenin signaling. In this review, we propose that the biophysical cues associated with three‐dimensional culturing could epigenetically reprogram HepG2 cells, thereby restoring the expression of crucial cytochrome P450 enzymes and related metabolizing proteins. This strategy may provide a more physiologically relevant hepatic model for drug metabolism and toxicity studies.
